According to Hardy-Scheulze rule, the coagulating power of an electrolyte will be higher for ionic components having greater charges or valencies.
For coagulating a sol of a particular charge, we add particles of opposite charge.
Thus, to coagulate antimony sulphide sol which is negatively charged, we must add an electrolyte with a cation of higher valency.
Thus, $\mathrm{Al}_2\left(\mathrm{SO}_4\right)_3$ that has $\mathrm{Al}^{3+}$, will be most effective for coagulating antimony sulphide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The plot of $\log \frac{x}{m}$ (y-axis) and $\log p(x$-axis) is a straight line inclined at an angle of $45^{\circ}$. When the intercept, $\mathrm{K}$ is 10 and pressure is $0.3 \mathrm{~atm}$ the amount of solute in grams adsorbed per gram of adsorbent $(\log 3=0.4771) ?$
questions.solution:
According to Freundlich adsorption isotherm:-
$\log \frac{x}{m}=\frac{1}{n} \log p+\log k(y=m x+c)$
We have, $\log \mathrm{k}=\log 10=1\log \mathrm{p}=\log (0.3)=-0.523\theta=45^{\circ} \text { so slope }=\frac{1}{n}=\tan \theta=\tan 45^{\circ}=1$
Thus, $\log \frac{\mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{m}}=(1)(-0.523)+1=0.4771\Rightarrow \quad \frac{x}{m}=3.0$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Assertion (A) Adsorption is an exothermic process.
Reason (R) Physisorption of a gas on a solid surface is normally reversible.
options: Both $A$ and $R$ are correct and $R$ is the correct. explanation of $\mathrm{A}$.
Both $A$ and $R$ are correct but $R$ is not the correct explanation of $\mathrm{A}$.
questions.solution:
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion. The correct reason for given assertion is as follows : When a gas is adsorbed on a solid surface, its movement is restricted. This leads to a decrease in the entropy of the gas i.e. $\Delta S$ is negative. Now, for a process to be spontaneous, $\Delta G$ should be negative.
We know that, $\Delta G=\Delta H-T \Delta S$
Now, $\Delta S$ is negative, $\Delta H$ has to be negative to make $\Delta G$ negative. Hence, adsorption is always exothermic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Freundlich adsorption isotherm fails at which of the following condition?
questions.solution:
The Freundlich adsorption isotherm is the mathematical representation for the variation of the extent of adsorption $(x / m)$ with pressure $(p)$ at a given temperature.

x / m=k \cdot p^{1 / n}(n>1)

where ' $x$ ' is the mass of the gas adsorbed on mass ' $m$ ' of the adsorbent at pressure ' $p$ '. ' $k$ ' and ' $n$ ' are constants that depend on the nature of the adsorbent and the gas at a particular temperature. Experimentally, it was determined that the extent of gas adsorption varies with pressure raised to the power $1 / n$ until saturation pressure $p_s$ is reached. At high pressure, $x / m$ becomes independent of pressure. Hence, Freundlich equation becomes

x / m=k \cdot p^0 \Rightarrow x / m=k

Thus, the Freundlich adsorption isotherm fails at higher pressure.

questions.solution:
( ( ) One of the most important properties of colloidal solutions is that colloidal particles possess a definite type of electrical charge. In a particular colloidal solution, all the colloidal particles carry the same type of charge, while the dispersion medium has an equal but opposite charge. Thus, the charge on colloidal particles is balanced by that of the dispersion medium and the colloidal solution as a whole is electrically neutral.
Positively charged sols are $\mathrm{TiO}_2, \mathrm{CdS}, \mathrm{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_3, \mathrm{SiO}_2$ Negatively charged sols are blood, $\mathrm{Cu}, \mathrm{Ag}$, clay.

questions.q:
The macromolecular colloids of the following are

I. Starch solution

II. Sulphur sol

III. Synthetic detergent

IV. Synthetic rubber
questions.solution: Macromolecules in suitable solvents form solutions in which the size of the macromolecules may be in the colloidal range. Such systems are called macromolecular colloids. These colloids are quite stable and resemble true solutions in many respects. Examples of naturally occurring macromolecules are starch, cellulose, proteins and enzymes; and those of man-made macromolecules are polythene, nylon, polystyrene, synthetic rubber, etc.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Assertion:- Animal skins are colloidal in nature

Reason:- Animal skin has positively charged particles.
options: Assertion is true. Reason is true and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion
Assertion is true. Reason is true but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false
Assertion is false but Reason is true
questions.solution: The sol particles acquire positive or negative charge by preferential adsorption of positive or negative ions. Animal hides are colloidal in nature. When a hide, which has positively charged particles, is soaked in tannin, which contains negatively charged colloidal particles, mutual coagulation takes place. This results in the hardening of leather. This process is termed as tanning.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The diameters range of colloidal particles is approximately.
questions.solution: A colloid is a heterogeneous system in which one substance is dispersed (dispersed phase) as very fine particles in another substance called dispersion medium. The essential difference between a solution and a colloid is that of particle size. While in a solution, the constituent particles are ions or small molecules, in a colloid, the dispersed phase may consist of particles of a single macromolecule (such as protein or synthetic polymer) or an aggregate of many atoms, ions or molecules. Colloidal particles are larger than simple molecules but small enough to remain suspended. Their range of diameters is between 1 and 1000 nm (10–9 to 10–6 m)

Photographic plates or films are prepared by coating an emulsion of the light sensitive silver bromide in gelatin over glass plates or celluloid films

Light sensitive property has allowed silver halides to become the basis of modern photographic materials

When silver bromide is exposed to sunlight, decomposition reaction takes place, which results in the formation of silver and bromine gas. This decomposition reaction is also called photochemical reactions, where white AgBr converts into grey colour silver in the presence of light

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which statements among the following are correct?
(i) Freundlich isotherm fails at high pressure of the gas.
(ii)ΔH<0 for both physical and chemical adsorption.
(iii) Physical adsorption is non-selective.
(iv) Chemical adsorption is reversible, where as physical adsorption is irreversible.
questions.solution:
According to the Freundlich isotherm, thevariation of extent of adsorption (x/m) with pressure (P) was given mathematically by Freundlich.Where n can take any whole number value which depends uponthe nature of adsorbate and adsorbent. The above relationship is
also called Freundlich’s adsorption isotherm.

xm=kP1n

At very high pressure, xm=k, it is independent of the pressure.

Physical adsorption (i.e. physisorption) :-

When the particles of the adsorbate are held to the surface of the adsorbent by the physical forces such as van der Waal’s forces, the adsorption is called physical adsorption or vanderwaals adsorption. Physical adsorption is non-selective. It is reversible and occur rapidly. It has the ∆H<0.
Chemical adsorption (i.e. chemisorption) :-
When the molecules of the adsorbate are held to the surface of the adsorbent by the chemical forces, the adsorption is called chemical adsorption. It is irreversible and occur slowly. It has the ∆H<0.

Hence, the statements (i),(ii)&(iii)only are correct.

questions.q: In an adsorption experiment, a graph between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>log</mi><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo>)</mo></math> versus <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>logP</mi></math> was found to be linear with a slope of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>45</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. According to the Freundlich's Adsorption Isotherm,

By taking the log both sides,

So, slope =1n⇒tan45°=1(n=1)

logK=0.3010⇒k=2

xm=2(0.5)1n xm=1

questions.q: The pressure exerted by a mixture of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of methane and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>CO</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> contained in a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi>dm</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math> flask at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>27</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> is

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A charcoal cube having side length \(10 \mathrm{~cm}\) is chopped lengthwise into 5 equal pieces. Then the effective adsorption power
questions.solution:
Initial volume of cube \(=(10)^3=1000 \mathrm{~cm}^3\)
\(V\) when cube is chopped along length then it will form cuboid in which length \(=6 \mathrm{~cm}\)
\(\begin{aligned}
\text {breadth } & =10 \mathrm{~cm} \\
\text {height } & =10 \mathrm{~cm}
\end{aligned}\)
Adsorption power \(\propto\) more surface area \(\propto 6 \mathrm{~cm}\)
\(\propto 6 \times(10)^2 \propto 600 \mathrm{~cm}^2\)
Final surface area of the cuboid
\(\begin{aligned}
& =2(l \times b+b \times h+h \times l) \text { Area of cuboid } \\
& =2(2 \times 10+100+20) \\
& =280 \mathrm{~cm}^2
\end{aligned}\)
For final cuboid area \(=280 \times 5=1400 \mathrm{~cm}^2\)
So, final adsorption power \(\propto 1400 \mathrm{~cm}^2\)
\(\begin{aligned}
\frac{\text { Final adsorption power }}{\text { Initial adsorption power }} & =\frac{1400}{600}=\frac{14}{6}=\frac{7}{3} \\
& =2.33 \text { times }
\end{aligned}\)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is correct for adsorption of solutes on solids in solutions?
options: The extent of adsorption increases with an increase in temperature
The extent of adsorption decreases with an increase of surface area of the adsorbate
The extent of adsorption decreases with an increase in temperature
The extent of adsorption does not depend on the amount of the solute in solution
questions.solution:
(a) The extent of adsorption increases with an increase in temperature is an incorrect statement because an increase in temperature reduces the interaction between the absorbate molecules and adsorbent molecules.
(b) The extent of adsorption decreases with an increase of surface area of the adsorbate is also an incorrect statement as adsorption $\propto$ surface area of adsorbate.
(c) The extent of adsorption decreases with an increased in temperature.

\because \text { Adsorption } \propto \frac{1}{\text { temperature }}

Thus, is the correct statement.
(d) The extent of adsorption does not depend on amount of solute in solution.
This is also an incorrect statement because :

\frac{x}{m} \propto \operatorname{conc} .(C)^{1 / n}

where, $\frac{x}{m}=$ amount of adsorbent $(x)$, adsorbed on given mass $(m)$ of adsorbate and $n=$ an integer. Thus, plot of $\log \frac{x}{m} v s \log C$ gives a straight line upward slope.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

Physical adsorption takes place with decrease of free energy whereas chemical adsorption occurs with increase of free energy
Physical adsorption requires low activation energy but chemical adsorption requires high activation energy
The magnitude of chemical adsorption increases and that of physical adsorption decreases with rise in temperature
questions.solution:
Both physical and chemical adsorption are exothermic in nature. But, chemical absorption requires high heat of adsorption due to formation of chemical bond.

Moreover, magnitude of chemical adsorption increases and that of physical adsorption decreases with the rise in temperature due to requirement of activation energy in case of chemical adsorption. Thus, option (b) is incorrect.

$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{KCl} \rightleftarrows \mathrm{K}^{+}+\mathrm{Cl}^{-} \\
& \mathrm{KNO}_3 \rightleftarrows \mathrm{K}^{+}+\mathrm{NO}_3^{-} \\
& \mathrm{K}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4 \rightleftarrows 2 \mathrm{~K}^{+}+\mathrm{NO}_4^{2-} \\
& \mathrm{K}_3\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right] \rightleftarrows 3 \mathrm{~K}^{-}+\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{3-}
\end{aligned}$
Hence, $\mathrm{K}_3\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]$ will be most effective in causing coagulation of ferric hydroxide solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following gives a straight line for Freundlich adsorption isotherm?
questions.solution: Freundlich adsorption isotherm is as $\frac{x}{m}=K p^{1 / n}$ Taking logarithms on both sides $\log \frac{x}{m}=\log K+\frac{1}{n} \log p$ On plotting a graph between $\log x / m$ and $\log p$, a straight line will be obtained.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A micelle formed during the cleansing action by soap is
options: aggregated particles of soap and dirt
an aggregated particle of dust and water
questions.solution: Soap contains hydrophobic (ie, fat soluble or water repelling) as well as hydrophilic (water soluble) end. Hydrophobic end remains soluble in dust or grease particles while hydrophilic end is attracted towards water. Hence, several hydrophobic pocket surrounds the grease particles. This aggregate of soap and dirt is called micelle. On washing with plenty of water dust is removed along with soap.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following is most effective in causing the coagulation of an $\mathrm{As}_2 \mathrm{~S}_3$ sol?
questions.solution: $\mathrm{As}_2 \mathrm{~S}_3$ is a negative sol. It is obvious that cations are effective in coagulating negative sols. According to Hardy Schulze rule, greater the valency of the coagulating ion, greater is its coagulating power. Thus, out of the given, $\mathrm{AlCl}_3\left(\mathrm{Al}^{3+}\right)$ is most effective for causing coagulation of $\mathrm{As}_2 \mathrm{~S}_3$ sol.
